text: The ocean stores heat, and the consequences can last for generations. A climate science synthesis released on October sixth highlights lasting ocean warming and sea level rise. The ocean absorbs excess heat, and deeper waters respond slowly. Some consequences persist over centuries, but their eventual scale still depends on how quickly emissions fall. This report brings together earlier research; it is not a new local flood forecast. The glacier footage is contextual archive, not this week's fieldwork. Cutting emissions still matters because every additional increment of warming adds risk. Follow for more science about our planet.
